The provider and the model actually support OpenAI-style function calling.
The backend is passing the functions argument and not just the system prompt.
Why llama4 is not making tool calls:
Most open-source Llama models (including Llama-2, Llama-3, and likely Llama-4) do not natively support OpenAI function calling out of the box, unless you are using a special fine-tuned version (like Llama-3-8B-Instruct with function-calling support).
Even with explicit instructions, the model will not emit the required tool call JSON unless it is specifically trained or fine-tuned to do so, or unless the backend is using a function-calling wrapper.

hi @Arjun 
Context

I’m running Rowboat (Docker) locally on Linux with Ollama + Phi-3, trying to use Ollama as the only LLM provider (no OpenAI at all).

Goal

Run Rowboat  + Copilot + Agents 100% on Ollama (Phi-3) using OpenAI-compatible mode.

Environment

OS: Linux

Docker + Docker Compose

Rowboat repo: https://github.com/rowboatlabs/rowboat

Ollama running locally (ollama serve)

Model: phi3:latest

✅ Ollama works perfectly:

curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions


Phi-3 responds correctly.

Key findings

Rowboat Web does NOT use LLM_PROVIDER

LLM_PROVIDER is ignored in Rowboat Web

Internally it always uses createOpenAI() from @ai-sdk/openai

Rowboat Web can work with Ollama

Ollama is OpenAI-compatible

Works when:

PROVIDER_BASE_URL points to Ollama

A dummy API key is provided

Critical gotcha

docker-compose.yml overrides .env

The following line was hardcoded and caused the issue:

PROVIDER_API_KEY: "ollama"


This caused "Incorrect API key provided" errors

✅ Fix:

PROVIDER_API_KEY: "sk-dummy-ollama-key"


Another blocker

MongoDB was already running on the host

Docker Mongo tried to bind to 27017 → restart loop

Fix: stop host Mongo or remove it

Current docker-compose (working so far)

services:
  rowboat:
    build:
      context: ./apps/rowboat
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    network_mode: host   # required to access local Ollama
    environment:
      PROVIDER_BASE_URL: "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
      PROVIDER_API_KEY: "sk-dummy-ollama-key"
      PROVIDER_DEFAULT_MODEL: "phi3:latest"
      PROVIDER_COPILOT_MODEL: "phi3:latest"
      OPENAI_API_KEY: "dummy"
      USE_AUTH: "false"

Thanks for the reply 🙏 here are the exact errors + observations we are seeing.

Context
- OS: Linux
- Rowboat Web (Docker, official repo)
- Ollama running locally
- Model: phi3:latest
- Goal: Rowboat Web + Ollama (with and without LiteLLM)

✅ Ollama works perfectly on its own
- curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags ✅
- curl /v1/chat/completions ✅
- Phi-3 responds correctly

----------------------------------
CASE 1 – Rowboat Web + Ollama (without LiteLLM)
----------------------------------

Config:
- LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
- PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434
- Dummy OPENAI_API_KEY

Observed error:
Rowboat backend still attempts OpenAI-style validation and fails with:
"Incorrect API key provided: dummy"

Root cause we found:
- docker-compose.yml had PROVIDER_API_KEY hardcoded to "ollama"
- Rowboat internally uses `createOpenAI(...)` even for Ollama
- This requires a dummy api key string (not empty, not "ollama")

After fixing PROVIDER_API_KEY, Rowboat starts correctly, BUT:
- Network issues appear if Ollama is accessed via container network
- Requires either:
  - network_mode: host
  - or host.docker.internal mapping

----------------------------------
CASE 2 – Rowboat Web + LiteLLM + Ollama
----------------------------------

We tried LiteLLM to fully follow the docs.

LiteLLM started via Docker:
- ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main
- config.yaml mounted with:

model_list:
  - model_name: ollama/phi3:latest
    litellm_params:
      model: ollama/phi3:latest
      api_base: http://host.docker.internal:11434

Problem:
LiteLLM ALWAYS loads internal Azure/OpenAI defaults and ignores config.yaml.

Observed logs:
- LiteLLM initializes AsyncAzureOpenAI
- Error:
  openai.OpenAIError: Missing credentials (AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY)
- Loaded config printed in logs always shows Azure GPT-4 examples,
  never the ollama model

This happens even when:
- config.yaml is mounted correctly
- no OpenAI/Azure keys are set
- using --network host
- using LITELLM_CONFIG env var

Result:
LiteLLM proxy never reaches Ollama and exits before serving /v1/models

conlusion 
- Ollama itself works ✅
- LiteLLM Docker image seems to fallback silently to Azure/OpenAI even when config is provided
- Rowboat Web CAN talk to Ollama directly, but the setup is very sensitive to:
  - hardcoded env vars in docker-compose
  - dummy API key handling
  - network mode

Happy to provide:
- docker-compose.yml
- litellm.yaml
- exact commands if you want to reproduce

Appreciate you trying to reproduce this on your side 🙌
